additional_info.subject: Note to L2
RE: ID0394947-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / R3 170001583] Delivering Max power 120KW CRM:00921001397
additional_info.body:
Hello Marc Koester,
Hope you are doing well.
We analyzed the logs, and I will explain this using the examples you provided the timestamp:
As you can see in this log, what matters here is that the
EV_TarCur[A]
matches the
EVSE_NowCur[A]
as much as possible.
So, what is happening here?
The EV (vehicle) is requesting the charger to provide 300.8 amperes, in accordance with ISO and DIN standards. The EVSE (charger) will attempt to supply as much current as possible.
However, the actual current provided may not match the EV's request due to several influencing factors, such as temperature, State of Charge (SoC), and battery health. To investigate further, we can check the following in the "Change Configuration" tab in SCB:
In this configuration, you can see that the outlet will not exceed 250A unless it enters BoostMode, which is capable of providing up to 400A, but only for a very short duration. Since the cable is not cooled (as indicated by the absence of "Cooling Cable" in the configuration), the decrease in current is completely normal.
The first picture follows the same logic, but in that case, the "TarCur" and "NowCur" values match properly. The issue in that scenario might be due to the cable heating up, which caused it to provide less current.
If you need further clarification on anything, please feel free to ask.
Regards,
Beerpal Singh
eMobility Support
